terms.definition: The idea that a digit's value depends on its position within a number.
terms.function: Gives each digit a place-based worth (ones, tens, hundreds, and so on).
terms.whereItIs: Shown by the block columns and written digits in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the foundation of writing, reading, and computing with numbers.

terms.definition: The first three place positions of a number, worth 100, 10, and 1 each.
terms.function: Tell what each digit contributes to the total value of the number.
terms.whereItIs: The three labeled columns in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the starting set of places for understanding all whole numbers.

terms.definition: A number system in which each place is ten times the one to its right.
terms.function: They make ten of a place into one of the next higher place.
terms.whereItIs: The scaling between the block columns.
terms.whyItMatters: Why our number system only needs ten digits to write any number.

terms.definition: Exchanging ten units of one place for a single unit of the next higher place.
terms.function: Turns piled-up ones into a ten, and tens into hundreds.
terms.whereItIs: The regroup animation in the ones-to-tens step.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what 'carrying' and 'borrowing' mean during adding and subtracting.

terms.definition: A number written as the sum of its place-value parts, e.g. 573 = 500 + 70 + 3.
terms.function: Breaks a number open to show exactly what each digit contributes.
terms.whereItIs: Visible as the per-column digit plates in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It makes the connection between written form and quantity crystal clear.
